pageCache.pageTitle: Homepage - Sherborne Abbey CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Sherborne Abbey CE Primary School -
'The school helps pupils become well-rounded and caring individuals' (Ofsted 2022)
'This is the day that The Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it' (Psalm 118:24)
'Pupils enjoy attending this inclusive and welcoming school' (Ofsted 2022)
Learners are cared for, and inspired to be their best, every day of their lives.
Welcome to Sherborne Abbey Primary School
On behalf of the children, the staff team and our Local Governing Body, I would like to bestow a very warm welcome to Sherborne Abbey CE Primary School! As a church school our Christian values underpin all aspects of school life and are the foundation of our welcoming and inclusive school community. We truly believe that:
‘This is the day that the Lord has made; Let us rejoice and be glad in it’
At Sherborne Abbey CE Primary School we value each and every one of our children as individuals, and every member of our team is committed to providing a rich learning environment. We embrace all areas of learning and are particularly proud of the fact that we fully celebrate success in sport, art and performing arts as important aspects of a child’s development, alongside an excellent foundation in English and Maths.
Our children benefit hugely from high quality teaching and learning provided by our very experienced team, a wide range of after school clubs, and wrap around childcare provision that enables working parents to juggle family life.
An integral part of being a church school for us, is to teach and encourage our children to live their lives with a moral compass, and use our Christian values to help our children understand how they can do the right thing every day.
I am very proud to be the Head of School here at Sherborne Abbey, and would love to show you around and let you experience a true Abbey welcome for yourself.
If you would like a small taste of what some of our week’s entail – do have a look at our Weekly News & Diary Dates tab as my Weekly Round-Up is added there every week.
Mrs Lisa Thompson (aka Mrs T 😊)
Keep up to date with our latest news on Facebook.
For all our up to date news, including Mrs T's Weekly Round-Ups, please see the Weekly News, Diary Dates & Class Info tab 😊
SIAMS report praises our strong Christian vision
Sherborne Abbey Primary School’s Christian vision has been highly praised following a recent SIAMS inspection. Psalm 118:24 “This is the day the Lord has made, let us rejoice and be glad in...
Sherborne Abbey CE Primary School is a large purpose built primary school situated on Lenthay Road in Sherborne. We have a beautiful school, with extensive grounds that include a pond and wildlife area, a forest school, sports pitches and hard courts, all set against the stunning backdrop of the Dorset countryside.
Our ethos at Sherborne Abbey is to celebrate and be glad in every day, and our visitors comment on the warm welcome they receive from everyone in the Abbey family.
Our aim is for all our children to leave us as happy, confident and independent individuals with a positive Christian outlook on life and the resilience to take on their next challenge.
I trust this website will give you a taste of our school, as well as providing up to date information for Parents/Carers, Pupils and our wider Community.
I do hope that you enjoy browsing through our website, and that you find the information you are looking for, but if there is anything you can’t find or that we can help with, please contact the school office directly to ask for further information, a free paper copy of information on the website, or to arrange a visit to experience a true Sherborne Abbey welcome 🙏.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wrap Around Care - Sherborne Abbey CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Wrap Around Care
Breakfast Club:
From September 2025, Breakfast Club runs in the school hall from 7:45am until the start of the school day. The cost is £5.50 per child per session.
The children are given a healthy breakfast between 7:45 and 8:20am and enjoy various activities before they are taken to their class before the beginning of the school day.
Bookings need to be made and paid for online, by 1pm on Wednesday for the following week.
In the interest of safeguarding, all children must be signed into Breakfast Club by an appropriate adult (on the school’s contact list).
Information about Eduspot
After School Childcare:
From Easter 2026, After School Childcare runs from 3.15- 5.15pm Monday to Thursday, and from 3.15 – 4.15pm on a Friday. We charge £5.50 per pupil per hourly session (you can book for 1 hour or 2 hours).
The children are collected from their classes and brought to After School Childcare (Reception and KS1 children to a room in the Reception base and KS2 children to the DT room) where they are registered. All children attending are given a healthy snack and enjoy various activities both inside and out.
Bookings need to be made and paid for online, by 1pm on Wednesday for the following week.
In the interest of safeguarding, all children must be signed out of After School Childcare by an appropriate adult (on the school’s contact list). Adults need to come to the Reception base via the Reception gates for collection (note, this is not the school office entrance).
Bookings:
If you would like to book a place for your child/children please go to the Eduspot (School Money) website to book and pay for your sessions: www.eduspot.co.uk
You will be asked to set your own password for the system.
We must stress that a late fee will be applied to any bookings after the 1pm Wednesday deadline. A late fee will also be applied if you collect your child later than your original booking time.
Please note that we cannot refund cancellations as we have already committed to our staffing for the week. The only exception is if we have to cancel your booking, or if you make your booking weeks in advance – in which case a refund will be given if it before our 1pm Wednesday deadline. Thank you for your understanding with this 🙏.

pageCache.text:
Curriculum
From September 2025 we have been using the highly regarded Cornerstones curriculum, chosen because it is ‘A sequenced curriculum rich in skills and knowledge. Perfect for those schools who want an ambitious, well-structured curriculum.’
For us at Sherborne Abbey, this allows us to ensure our standards are high, whilst meeting the educational and creative needs of our lovely children and supporting teacher creativity and imagination. Amendments and adjustments can be made through the year to ensure that we adapt to the needs of our children, the interests of different cohorts and of course, local influences. However Cornerstones allows us to ensure a comprehensive coverage for our young people.
Due to the fact that we almost always have some mixed aged classes in school, we operate a 2 year cycle of themes in all phases so that pupils do not repeat content unless planned.
Our Curriculum Overview
So, what is the Cornerstones Curriculum and why is it beneficial?
https://cornerstoneseducation.co.uk/cornerstones-curriculum/
https://cornerstoneseducation.co.uk/cornerstones-curriculum/pedagogy/
The Cornerstones Curriculum is a creative and thematic approach to learning that is mapped to the 2014 primary national curriculum to ensure comprehensive coverage of national expectations.
It is based on a child-centred pedagogy called The Four Cornerstones and is delivered through Imaginative Learning Projects (ILPs) and Knowledge Rich Projects (KRPs), which provide a rich menu of exciting and motivating learning activities that make creative links between all aspects of children’s learning. We believe children learn better when they are encouraged to use their imagination and apply their learning to engaging contexts. Our curriculum provides many learning challenges throughout the academic year that require children to solve problems, apply themselves creatively and express their knowledge and understanding effectively. Cornerstones also provide a rigorous skills and knowledge framework that outlines the end of year expectations in all subjects.
These skills and knowledge are tied to activities and are age-related so that staff can track children’s progress and identify their individual learning needs.
Foundational Skills Approach
We believe that strong foundations in reading, writing, spelling and handwriting open the door to all future learning.
This policy explains how we support children — from their first phonics lesson through to confident, fluent reading and writing in Key Stage 2 — using approaches recommended in:
The Reading Framework The Writing Framework The National Curriculum
National guidance emphasises that systematic phonics, fluent handwriting, secure spelling and strong language skills create the “firm foundations” children need to succeed throughout school.
English & Literacy Skills
At Sherborne Abbey Primary School, we aim to develop each child’s ability to speak, listen, read and write effectively. A minimum of an hour each day is devoted to developing vital literacy skills, which are also used and practised in many ways across the whole curriculum.
Our children learn by actively engaging with a broad range of texts – from poetry to newspaper reports, mystery stories to letters of complaint. They read and write a wide variety of genres and, in doing so, learn how to communicate in the most effective way. Whether it is the youngest children experimenting with a story mat or the Year 6 children recording each other in video advertisements, we hope to make literacy fun and exciting, encouraging a love of books and the ability to share their thoughts, feelings and knowledge with others.
This journey begins in our Reception (Foundation) year through the use of high-quality phonics teaching. For this we use the highly regarded scheme – ELS (Essential Letters & Sounds).
The aim of ELS is ‘Getting all children to read well, quickly’. It teaches children to read by identifying the phonemes (smallest unit of sound) and graphemes (the written version of the sound) within words and using these to read words.
Children are taught phonics from the very beginning of Reception where it is explicitly taught every day during a dedicated slot in the timetable. Children are given the knowledge and the skills to then apply this independently. These daily sessions continue into KS1 and beyond for pupils who do not pass the phonic check before they transition to KS2.
Throughout the scheme, children learn to read and write the ‘harder to read and spell’ words which are listed below, alongside some further useful information about ELS:
This strong phonics knowledge is extended in Year 2 through Essential Spelling, which reinforces and deepens understanding while introducing children to broader patterns, rules and strategies.
From Key Stage 2, the progression continues through Essential Spelling and Word Knowledge, where the focus develops beyond simple spelling rules into a richer understanding of how words work. Pupils explore morphology, including prefixes, suffixes and root words, alongside spelling patterns and etymology.
Once children have mastered the foundations of reading, we know that helping them develop a love of reading is the best way forward to ensure academic success in all areas. Because of this we have completely overhauled our reading system to focus on making reading a basic skill for all, and every morning at Abbey starts with a focus on reading.
Further information about our approach can be found here:
We also use the Accelerated Reader scheme for children in Years 3 to 6, as we find the children enjoy the quizzes and independent element of this reading, and it helps our parents understand their child’s reading journey.
The final piece of our Reading jigsaw is our curriculum map for Reading where we map out our reading for every year group, ensuring that we have a wide range of genre included and specify the skills we are teaching. This is our Year 6 map.
In line with the recent Writing Framework, our ultimate ambition is for our children to become successful writers, writing with fluency and flair for a variety of reasons, and our revised Writing Plan reflects this. To ensure children have the foundational skills to be able to write fluently and with ease, we ensure that handwriting is a regular feature of our week with all classes starting the afternoon this way.
Our PenPals Overview shows how this works from Reception through to Year 6.
Our overall aim for English is to ensure that our children understand the importance of reading for both knowledge and pleasure; writing for a purpose, as well as to entertain; and speaking with confidence – being able to articulate their thoughts and feelings successfully.
Details of how we implement writing can be found here:
At Sherborne Abbey Primary School, we follow the White Rose scheme for our maths, and this enables us to develop each child’s ability to be mathematically proficient. A minimum of an hour each day is devoted to developing vital mathematical skills, which are also used and practised in many ways across the whole curriculum.
We are fortunate that as part of SAST we have worked closely with our partner schools to create a maths calculation policy that ensures coverage and continuity in maths from our Reception year through to Year 13.
CURRICULUM INTENT, CURRICULUM LEADERSHIP & CHAMPIONS
Further information about our curriculum is detailed here in our Curriculum Intent & Implementation documents.
Curriculum leadership at Sherborne Abbey CE Primary School is monitored and led by our Senior Leadership Team, with subjects allotted to subject champions who oversee, develop, monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of their subject within our school.
Our subject champions are carefully chosen because of their expertise, enthusiasm and experience.
We know that learning is not restricted to the classroom and we regularly enhance the children’s learning with visiting speakers and workshops, external visits from museums, zoos and local industry to ensure that our children can be inspired. One of the ways in which we monitor this is by using our in-house Abbey Activity Passport. This is based upon the 2018 Activity Passports introduced by Damian Hinds (then Secretary of State for Education). Mr Hinds asked everyone he met what they wanted for their children. The instinctive answer that came back was never about the curriculum or qualifications, as important as these are. What parents wanted first and foremost was for their child to be happy and healthy.
Mr Hinds agreed with this as a father, and as Education Secretary, that’s what he wanted for all children in this country. (Of course, he also wanted them to be safe and cared for, to have a world-class education and to make a successful transition to adulthood, to be fully equipped grown-ups, active members of society and to get a job and be able to provide for themselves and, in time, their own children.)
BUT MORE IMPORTANTLY, he wanted more than that for our children. He wanted them to lead a fulfilling life, to enjoy learning, to read for pleasure, to be excited by music and drama, to be curious about the world and people around them. He regularly heard from teachers that it’s important that children have the chance to try things out, to get a taste of the world around them, to see and do things that they wouldn’t normally do, or go to places they wouldn’t normally go and to meet people they wouldn’t normally meet.
These things are important because a world-class education is about much more than qualifications: it’s also about your character and wellbeing. Character is developed from taking on challenges and pursuing interests, by doing things that are worth doing even when they are difficult and which may not give an immediate reward.
That’s why Activity Passports were produced to cover a range of activities which it was believed children would enjoy and learn from, and as a school we wholly endorse this.
We know that our children have had a very strange few years (as have their families), and before the pandemic many of our families would have engaged in a similar venture with the National Trust’s ’50 things to do before you’re 11 ¾’ list. So we have created an Abbey Activity Passport that reflects the enriched curriculum here, and ensures a greater array of cultural capital for all our children regardless of their family circumstances, or indeed national circumstance!
One of the incredible learning experiences for our Year 6 children is their residential trip to Pendarren in the Brecon Beacons. Please do see our Year 6 class pages for further details of this residential which is so much more than a trip – it’s really a celebration of resilience, teamwork and personal growth. By the end of their week, the children return to school and family with greater confidence, stronger friendships, and a sense of achievement that they carry into their final year of primary school and beyond.
We also have an excellent array of extra curricular clubs provided by professionals in their field (art/football/dance etc), as well as clubs run by our staff team to expose children to skills they may not have experienced before (sewing/knitting/ballroom dance etc).
As part of our Cornerstones Curriculum we also begin each new topic with a memorable experience intended to engage the children in their learning and give them a spark of excitement to stimulate their curiosity. This might be a visit from Lyme Regis museum to bring Mary Anning to life, or a Viking Day to truly appreciate the wonder of that time.

School News 19 September 2024
SIAMS report praises our strong Christian vision
Sherborne Abbey Primary School’s Christian vision has been highly praised following a recent SIAMS inspection. Psalm 118:24 “This is the day the Lord has made, let us rejoice and be glad in it” is the basis for their Christian vision, and it sits at the forefront of decision making and actions within the school.
The Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools (SIAMS) report says “the Christian vision inspires adults and pupils to seize the daily opportunities that are provided” and the “way that the Christian vision has been refreshed ensures it meaningfully addresses the needs of the school community.”
It goes on to say that “Pupils are polite, courteous and thoughtful” and that “the recent change in language from behaviour to relationships, reflects the importance of positive interactions in the school”. SAST was also praised by inspectors, who said “The vision of the trust and school closely align, generating a powerful shared drive to ensure adults and pupils thrive. Leaders embrace the training opportunities offered by SAST and the diocese, and work with determination to develop the school as a Church school”.
The school proudly sits at the heart of the community and embraces the wider role it has to play. The report recognised this “As a practical outworking of the vision, the school acts as a community hub. It hosts meetings with social care, health and education as well as providing a community supermarket and foodbank. Through these effective partnerships between the school and local providers, pupils and families can access additional assistance when required.”
It is not just pupils who are benefiting from the school’s strong Christian ethos, staff are too, with inspectors highlighting “Teamwork in the school is strong and staff feel valued and valuable. They are given the opportunity to grow in their roles through professional development and training. Reflecting the Christian vision and the value of compassion, all members of the school community are treated well.”
Executive Headteacher Ian Bartle said “Sherborne Abbey Primary School is incredibly proud of our Christian School status and upholding our values, which are very dear to us all. It is through the amazing work of our dedicated staff team, relationships with our supportive parents and carers, links with our Trust, and our wonderful children, that we could make this happen”.
Sarah Willoughby, who leads SAST’s Church Schools Flourishing Programme said “This SIAMS report pays testament to the hard work and dedication of not only the school’s leadership team, but also the entire school community who have come together and proudly shared what makes a strong Church School.”

Dojo/Parent apps
CLASS DOJO * Class Dojo is a secure platform that teachers, children and families can use every day to build a close-knit community. * Learning and experiences at school (and home) can be shared through photos, videos and messages. * It is secure and personal to our school. * Parents/carers can easily join using any device. * Class Dojo instantly translates messages into 30+ languages.
It’s a little like school Facebook, but completely secure and each class has a separate section.
We ❤️ Class Dojo, but please note that it should only be used for classroom based quick queries. For anything important, sensitive or timely please still email the office to ensure an appropriate response. Please also note that the team will not be able to respond on Class Dojo before 8.15am or after 5pm during school days. They are also understandably committed with your children throughout the school day, but do try and keep tabs on it.
Stories Stories are instantly updating streams of messages, pictures and videos similar to a social media-style timeline. Every class and school has their own Story, all of which are shared home with all parents/carers. Class Story helps teachers to share photos, messages, updates with all families connected to their class, whilst the School Story regularly shares Community News, along with a Weekly Round Up from Mrs T on a Friday.
Messages Messages allow teachers and parents to instantly message each other, without needing to share phone numbers or contact details. Messages can be translated into 30+ different languages, and “Quiet Hours” lets teachers set away times so parents know when they are not available. Messages sent out of hours will not be seen by the teacher until the next working day. Our quiet hours are before 8.15am, and after 5pm. You are welcome to message in our quiet times, but please note that you will not get a response.
Dojo Points Teachers use Class Dojo to promote positive behaviours in their classroom. Each child gets a monster avatar, and teachers can award Dojos for things such as staying on task, showing excellent manners, fantastic teamwork or brilliant homework.
Children can choose to save their Dojos and spend them on bigger prizes/experiences or spend them straight away for smaller rewards/experiences. Children across the school are actively involved in setting up prizes and experiences for the Dojo shop….they love spending their Dojos, as you can see!
WHAT DOES IT MEAN FOR YOU AS A PARENT/CARER? Connecting with your child’s teacher on ClassDojo will allow you to do the following:
You will receive a unique email that will allow you to connect to your child’s class and teacher. Once you have created a parent account, teachers will be able to send you a unique code or link for your child’s account that will give them access to a pupil account, Class Story and School Story.
Class Dojo can be used on any device – it’s a simple, free mobile app for iOS and Android (please do not pay for upgraded version), and can also be accessed from your computer at classdojo.com.

SEND
‘Our vision for children with special educational needs and disabilities is the same as for all children and young people – that they achieve well in their early years, at school and in college, and lead happy and fulfilled lives.’ (Department for Education)
At Sherborne Abbey School, we are committed to offering an inclusive curriculum to ensure the best possible progress for all of our pupils whatever their needs or abilities. Our emphasis is on a whole school approach, and all staff accept responsibility for providing all children with realistic learning goals in a broad-based, appropriate curriculum.
We are especially good at providing a nurturing environment, and developing the educational, social, emotional, cultural and spiritual aspects for all our children through our curriculum design and teaching approaches.
Our Head of School, Mrs Thompson, is a trained SENDCo and works closely alongside our lovely SENDCo – Ms Beaumont.
The National Curriculum Council stated that participation in the National Curriculum by pupils with special educational needs is most likely to be achieved by encouraging good practice for all pupils and that the majority of pupils with learning difficulties simply require work to be suitably presented and differentiated to match their need.
Ms Kirsty Beaumont can be contacted via the school office. Please note that she does not work full time, so there may be a short delay in coming back to you.

Governance
Our Local Governing Body (LGB) @ Sherborne Abbey 😊:
The Governors responsibility is to monitor and scrutinise teaching and learning, welfare, and safeguarding issues. Governors provide challenge and support to the Headteachers and Senior Leadership Team, and represent the Trust to local stakeholders – parents, students, staff and the community. Two representatives of each LGB are elected from among that school’s parents, while a further representative will be elected by the staff. The Headteacher is ex officio. The remaining representatives are appointed by the Trustees following recommendation from the LGB and Headteacher, based on skills and experience, or in our Church of England academies, the Diocese of Salisbury and the Diocese of Bath & Wells receive and consider nominations and appoint.
Ex ‘VA’ schools must have a majority of foundation representatives and ex ‘VC’ 25% of representatives must be foundation. Each AR is appointed for a term of four years, after which time, LGB representatives, with agreement from the Diocese or Trustees, may agree to renewal of further term(s).
Our Governors meet at the beginning of each full term (three times a year), plus an additional meeting in July to review published exam performance.

Our meetings run from 4 – 5.30pm.

The Local Governing Body’s Representatives can be contacted in writing: c/o Rev Lesley McCreadie, Chair of Governors, at the school or by email to office@sherborneabbey.dorset.sch.uk
Effective governance underpins all successful and strong Multi-Academy Trusts (MATs). SAST has a three-tier governance system and each layer has distinct responsibility and power set out out in a Scheme of Delegation.
SAST’s Scheme of Delegation explains how the above core responsibilities are delivered through its Members, Board of Trustees and Academy Committees.
Our priority is to support every school in providing excellent education while ensuring it remains a key part of its community.
There is a balance as to the responsibilities delegated to schools and those that are the responsibility of SAST. The focus is to continually evaluate, improve and develop through strong, effective and accountable leadership at all levels. The aim is to establish clear, simple and effective accountability including slim and streamlined governance.
There are three levels of governance:
Members:– Members appoint the Trustees to run SAST, and are the only people able to amend the Articles of Association of the SAST. There are 4 members of which 2 will be Diocese Board of Education representatives (Salisbury, and Bath and Wells) in a corporate capacity and 1 other with foundation status. Members have a strategic vision, with a range of skills such as academic/education, financial, legal, corporate business and creative/cultural.
Board of Trustees:- Trustees determine policy, and make decisions for the SAST. They are the statutory Governing Body of each School. There is capacity for 12 Trustees including 6 with foundation status. The Trustees are appointed on the basis of the skills balance required for the SAST including finance, legal, HR, project/business management, education and estates.
Local Governing Body (LGB):- Each school has a local Governing Body with agreed delegation to respond to the context, status, needs and resources of its school community and its connections to the wider world. The Governors will focus on teaching and learning, standards and achievement, community and safeguarding. There can be up to 12 representatives in each school and its composition reflects its previous VC, VA or community status. There will be no local level sub-committees.

Safeguarding
Our Safeguarding Statement
At Sherborne Abbey CE Primary School, there is nothing more important to us than the physical and emotional health and well-being of our pupils and staff alike. We recognise that every day we are trusted with the most precious members of your families. As such we have created and work hard to maintain a climate in which staff, pupils, parents and governors feel able to articulate concerns comfortably; safe in the knowledge that effective action will be taken, as appropriate.
Our Safeguarding Policies apply to all adults, including volunteers, working in, or on behalf of our School. We expect everyone working in or for our school to share responsibility for keeping children safe from harm and abuse and report any concerns to one of our DSLs (please see below). Together we must ensure that all children, their families and our staff, feel safe, valued and cared for at all times and are nurtured to thrive and achieve to be the best we can be.
We welcome volunteers, including parents, into our school but at all times ensure that volunteers are suitable to work with children. Those who volunteer to spend time with our children on a regular basis are required to undergo a DBS check.
At Sherborne Abbey, children are taught about how to stay safe physically, mentally and spiritually. This includes staying safe online. Our taught curriculum and PSHE programme of assemblies covers how to stay physically and emotionally healthy and includes e-safety and age-appropriate sex and relationship education (SRE). We use Jigsaw to ensure good coverage and age appropriate resources and content.
All concerns regarding our children, whether relating to safeguarding, behaviour, home life etc are recorded electronically using a programme called My Concern.
Designated Safeguarding Leads – DSLs
The school’s Designated Safeguarding Lead is Mrs Lisa Thompson – Head of School. She is supported by Deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads/Links:
Operation Encompass is a police and education early information safeguarding partnership enabling schools to offer immediate support to children experiencing domestic abuse. Mrs Lisa Thompson is our primary contact for Dorset Police and Operation Encompass.
Beyond the School Day:
Mrs Hayley Harris (Breakfast and After School Childcare Lead) is the extended schools Safeguarding Link and Mrs Lisa Thompson (Head of School) is the DSL.
Any of the above people can be contacted if you are worried about your own home situation or that of any other child. You can do so in confidence by making an appointment via the school office to see the Head of School or phoning on 01935 812318.
ALL our staff have been trained on safeguarding to the appropriate requirements.
Mr Daniel Hutchings is the Designated Safeguarding Academy Committee representative (Governor).
Recruitment/Volunteering
Sherborne Abbey Primary School is committed to protect our children. ALL POSTS will require an enhanced disclosure barring service check prior to appointment / working with our children. This will be carried out by the school prior to appointment. DBS checks will be completed again every 4 years in rotation. All staff will complete annual Safeguarding training and a yearly SAST wide Declaration Form.
School Security and Safety
Our purpose built school was constructed with security in mind.
Adult access (visitors, parents, contractors etc.) is only available through the main entrance, which has a controlled entry system and all other doors and gates are locked at 8.45am to ensure our children’s safety throughout the school day.
Health and Safety is of upmost importance to us. We are regularly audited by Dorset Council and the Department for Education.
Cars are allowed onto site at morning drop off but access is severely restricted at home-time to ensure children can leave our site safely without the risk of moving cars and fumes. Please note that any abuse of this might result in your car being banned from our private site.
If you are a blue badge holder, please speak to the office to request your Red Badge/Home-time Parking Permit. ONLY cars with this permit are allowed onto site between 2.30pm & 3.30pm each day.
We are also fortunate enough to be working with Fernao Barros, Community Engagement Officer at Dorset Council, for their School Streets initiative.
Worried About a Child’s Safety?
If you are concerned about a child in Dorset and want to speak to someone, contact the Children’s Advice and Duty Service on 01305 228558 and give as much info as you can.

pageCache.text:
EYFS/Reception
Our two Reception classes are Caterpillars & Ladybirds and are taught by Mrs Harrison and Mrs Guiver respectively (please note that occasionally one of these classes may be a mixed year group with Year 1 children depending upon numbers).
Our learning is centred around play, but with a rigorous phonics scheme – Essential Letters & Sounds (ELS).
PLEASE BE AWARE THAT WE USE CLASS DOJO TO SHARE ALL OUR CLASS LEARNING, PHOTOS AND COMMUNICATION DIRECTLY WITH OUR FAMILIES, THEREFORE THESE CLASS PAGES SIMPLY PROVIDE USEFUL LINKS TO AID, SUPPORT & ENHANCE LEARNING AT HOME 😊
Useful Online Resources to Support Your Child’s Learning
Please find below a list of useful websites where you will be able to access books online for free:
Reading Amazon Audible
Amazon Audible have made all stories free to stream. Encourage children to download a story of their choice to keep them hearing books aloud. You will need to select the littlest listeners or elementary where some of these will be appropriate for year 2. Audible Stories: Free Audiobooks for Kids | Audible.com
The Book Trust have created the Book Trust Cupboard. Here you will find lots of activities to complete with your child as well as online stories. Open the HomeTime Cupboard for fun how to draw videos, stories and activities
https://www.booktrust.org.uk
This website has been made free to use again. We use this resource in school and your children are familiar with it. Practising phonic knowledge daily will help your child become a fluent reader.
https://www.phonicsplay.co.uk
Reading Eggs are providing a free 30 day trial. You will have to sign up and to begin with it will ask your child to complete a series of activities to find the correct level for them.
https://readingeggs.co.uk/
Cbeebies Full of playful and imaginative stories.
https://www.bbc.co.uk/cbeebies/stories
Teach Your Monster to Read
A free game that makes learning to read fun. Read for pleasure. Collect books and go on quests that ignite a love of reading.
https://www.teachyourmonster.org/
An interactive resource that covers a range of Mathematic skills that will improve your child’s Maths knowledge.
Classroom Secrets Kids
Is a tailored programme which is an interactive learning platform for children. It complements the curriculum while allowing them to push themselves further. Free 14 day trial.
http://www.kids.classroomsecrets.co.uk
Primary Early Years (and Other) Interactive Games
Activities to support all areas of Early Years Learning
http://www.primaryinteractive.co.uk/
